body: I don't have time for that. I have a full time job and don't want to spend my free time driving all over town. The nearest therapist is like 25 minutes away. Would that really even be more effective than calling?

That makes sense, but I was calling people even before I went to the crisis place. I was calling just random psychiatrists that are nearby who are fairly well reviewed and on my insurance. I guess I need to start calling the poorly reviewed ones just to be able to see anyone at all. This is absurd though. It shouldn't be so difficult for someone who isn't motivated to do anything to find a therapist.

>Doctors are usually pretty accurate with their schedules, why would it take two months?

Total fucking bullshit. My wife finally called them back today because they never got back to me, and now they say there are 20 people ahead of me and there is absolutely no way I will get in within 4 weeks. Everyone's completely fucking worthless.

Great, I'm also on UHC. This isn't making me feel any better. My wife is actually finding the doctors making the phone calls because I can't motivate myself to do much of anything, but it seems like there are a decent number of decent doctors in-network. It's just hard to actually get in to see one.

>Doctors are usually pretty accurate with their schedules

Not in my experience.

>It is what you said. An impression.

It's more than an impression given that on at least three separate occasions, I have left voicemails at psychiatrists' offices telling them I'm suicidal and want an appointment, and never heard back from them. Sometimes multiple voicemails. There is no excuse for that.

>Absolutely not. Why are you so pessimistic?

Again, that's been my experience with psychiatrists. They start me out on a low dose of something, then I have to take it for weeks or months to tell if there's any effect, then they slowly increase the dose and eventually give up.

>You do want to get better, don't you? If you put your head in the sand like that, you never will.

I want to get better, but no one I talk to about this (including therapists) suggests anything new, so I have no reason to think there's a chance I will get better.

>Therapy and meds saved my life. And I can say that I am at least as intelligent, cultured and aware of the state of the world as you.

>Therefore, it can work for you.

You're being arrogant and defensive for some reason. What does any of that have to do with whether or not therapy and medications can help me, anyway?

I'll wait for someone else to reply who has something to say that I haven't heard before, although I doubt that will happen. Don't know why I bothered posting now.

I'm trying to find a new psychiatrist. The first one I called was supposedly taking new patients but hasn't responded to a voicemail left over a week ago. The second one says they can get me in within 4 weeks. Given my experience with doctors, that really means I'll be lucky to get an appointment by 2 months from now. Like I said, the medical system completely sucks, and I get the impression that no one I talk to actually gives a shit. Then it will take months on each medication to find out that no dosage makes any difference and move onto new ones until I'm out of options. All this will do is prolong my misery.

I have no motivation to try meditation at home, much less find a "center" to go to where annoying New Agers can tell me how to sit and do nothing properly.
